title: Chemistry: From Atoms to Reactions
summary: Audio-first chemistry from atomic structure, reactions and molecular mechanisms through chemical measurement, materials and electronic solids to semiconductors, solar cells, light-emitting devices, molecular excited states, photocatalysis and photosynthesis. Each lecture has a scientific companion and source-linked claims.
assumed_background: Everyday familiarity with materials, temperature and mixing. Fractions, ratios and unit conversions are explained through examples. Formal quantum mechanics, calculus and prior chemistry are not assumed.

lectures.title: What Is a Substance? The Chemical Identity of Matter
lectures.description: Distinguishes compounds, elements, mixtures and phase changes through separation and mass accounting, then asks how chemical identity can be inferred from measurements.

lectures.title: The Periodic Table Is a Map of Electrons
lectures.description: Explains recurring elemental properties using nuclear charge, electron states, screening and valence electrons; reconstructs how Mendeleev’s predictions and Moseley’s X-ray measurements justified the table.

lectures.title: Why Atoms Stay Together: Bonds, Shapes, and Materials
lectures.description: Builds chemical bonding from energy and electron density, distinguishes molecular, ionic and metallic materials, and explains how geometry changes polarity and bulk properties.

lectures.title: Water and the Chemistry of Dissolving
lectures.description: Explains why salt, sugar and oil behave differently in water using solvation, molecular polarity, Gibbs energy, saturation, electrolytes and colligative effects.

lectures.title: Counting the Invisible: Moles, Equations, and Limiting Reactants
lectures.description: Connects chemical formulas to measured masses through the SI mole, balanced reactions, limiting-reactant arithmetic, percent yield and concentration measurements.

lectures.title: Where the Reaction Energy Goes: Heat, Entropy, and Chemical Direction
lectures.description: Separates bond energy from net reaction heat, explains enthalpy and calorimetry, and develops entropy, Gibbs energy, equilibrium and kinetic persistence.

lectures.title: The Reaction Has a Clock: Rates, Temperature, and Evidence
lectures.description: Reads chemical reaction rates from concentration-time observations, experimental orders and temperature dependencies while separating intrinsic kinetics from mixing and transport.

lectures.title: The Other Route Through a Reaction: Mechanisms and Catalysts
lectures.description: Examines intermediate species, multistep reaction mechanisms, catalytic cycles, enzyme saturation, surface chemistry and evidence used to discriminate pathways.

lectures.title: Equilibrium Is Still Moving: Reaction Quotients and Chemical Balance
lectures.description: Builds equilibrium from reversible chemistry, Q and K, chemical potentials, activity corrections, gas pressure, phase changes and nonequilibrium steady states.

lectures.title: What Acidity Measures: Protons, Water, and Chemical Speciation
lectures.description: Explains conjugate acid-base pairs, weak versus strong acids, pH activity, autoionization, carbonate speciation and why alkalinity differs from pH.

lectures.title: Why a Buffer Resists Change: Weak Acids, Titrations, and Chemical Capacity
lectures.description: Develops buffer action, finite capacity, Henderson–Hasselbalch calculations and the distinction among half-equivalence, equivalence and indicator endpoints.

lectures.title: How Chemistry Produces Voltage: Electrons, Ions, and Galvanic Cells
lectures.description: Connects redox reactions and ionic return paths to cell voltage, Gibbs energy, the Nernst relation, battery capacity, corrosion and historical galvanic cells.

lectures.title: Forcing Chemistry with Electricity: Electrolysis, Batteries, and Selectivity
lectures.description: Develops externally driven redox chemistry, thermodynamic versus operating voltages, Faraday charge accounting, plating, water electrolysis, efficiency and charging limits.

lectures.title: Carbon Is a Framework: Chains, Rings, and Shared Electrons
lectures.description: Builds organic structures from four-valent carbon, skeletal formulas, constitutional isomers, conformations, alkene geometry and aromatic electron delocalization.

lectures.title: What a Functional Group Changes: From Alcohols to Amides
lectures.description: Uses hydrogen bonding, proton transfer, carbonyl polarization and resonance to distinguish alcohols, ethers, amines, acids, esters and amides.

lectures.title: When Molecules Have Handedness: Isomers in Three Dimensions
lectures.description: Explains constitutional and stereo-isomerism, chiral tetrahedral centers, optical rotation, R/S and E/Z labels, meso molecules and molecular recognition through Pasteur tartrate evidence.

lectures.title: Follow the Electron Pair: How to Read an Organic Reaction
lectures.description: Introduces electron-pair curved arrows, nucleophiles, electrophiles, formal charge, proton transfers, carbonyl attack, resonance versus intermediates, and tests of mechanism.

lectures.title: One Carbon, Four Pathways: Substitution and Elimination
lectures.description: Compares SN2, SN1, E2 and E1 using observed rate laws, leaving-group ability, solvent effects, stereochemical inversion, carbocation rearrangement, and anti-periplanar elimination.

lectures.title: The Two Lives of a Carbonyl: Addition and Acyl Substitution
lectures.description: Distinguishes aldehyde/ketone addition from carboxylic-acid-derivative acyl substitution; develops reduction, esterification, hydrolysis, amide resistance, catalysis and peptide links.

lectures.title: When Molecules Become Materials: Polymer Chains and Their Properties
lectures.description: Explains chain-growth and step-growth polymerization, molecular-size distributions, stoichiometric conversion, glass transitions, crystalline regions, elastomers, crosslinks and environmental degradation.

lectures.title: The Sample Is Not the World: What Chemical Measurement Actually Represents
lectures.description: Develops the measurand, representative sampling, filtered versus total material, spatial and temporal variability, sample preservation, matrix effects and field blanks.

lectures.title: Turning a Signal into a Number: Calibration, Detection, and Uncertainty
lectures.description: Explains calibration curves, sample dilution, matrix-matched and internal standards, blanks, detection and quantification limits, precision, bias, and measurement uncertainty.

lectures.title: When Light Measures Matter: Absorption, Color, and Fluorescence
lectures.description: Builds UV/visible absorbance and Beer–Lambert reasoning from photons, transmittance and path length, then explains multicomponent spectra and fluorescence limits.

lectures.title: The Bonds Are Moving: Infrared and Raman Fingerprints
lectures.description: Explains molecular normal modes, infrared dipole selection rules, Raman polarizability, FTIR, ATR surface sensitivity, spectral fingerprinting and mixture ambiguity.

lectures.title: Listening to Atomic Nuclei: How NMR Reveals Molecular Structure
lectures.description: Develops spin resonance, shielding, chemical shift, integration, coupling, proton and carbon NMR, Fourier-transform acquisition and structural inference.

lectures.title: A Mixture Enters a Column: The Logic of Chromatography
lectures.description: Explains differential retention, chromatography modes, TLC, GC, LC, peak resolution, coelution, detection, and the development of plant-pigment separations.

lectures.title: Weighing Ions, Not Molecules: What a Mass Spectrum Can Tell Us
lectures.description: Explains m/z and charge states, electron and electrospray ionization, isotopic patterns, accurate mass, tandem MS, matrix effects and limits of spectral database matches.

lectures.title: Building the Chemical Case: How Independent Measurements Become Evidence
lectures.description: Integrates sampling, blanks, chromatography, UV detection, MS identity, extraction recovery, uncertainty and evidence limits in a worked fictional water investigation.

lectures.title: A Map of What Matter Can Be: Phase Diagrams and Chemical Equilibrium
lectures.description: Builds pure-substance and binary phase maps using chemical potential, vapor pressure, triple and critical points, the phase rule and a lever-rule alloy calculation.
tag_paths: Binary phase diagrams and lever rule

lectures.title: How a Crystal Begins: Nucleation, Growth, and Defects
lectures.description: Explains surface-energy barriers to nucleation, heterogeneous seeds, supersaturation, grain growth, polymorphs and how defects alter materials.

lectures.title: The Solid That Never Crystallized: Glass and the Race Against Time
lectures.description: Shows how supercooling, structural arrest, relaxation and thermal history produce amorphous glasses with distinct optical and mechanical properties.

lectures.title: The Ceramic Is Not Just Clay: Pores, Sintering, and Microstructure
lectures.description: Connects powder processing, diffusion-driven neck formation, densification, grain growth, ceramic defect chemistry and brittle fracture to applications.
tag_paths: Ceramic defect chemistry and ion transport

lectures.title: The Chemistry of the Edge: Surfaces, Wetting, and Adsorption
lectures.description: Explains surface free energy, contact-angle balance, capillary flow, adsorption, active surface sites and practical coating or catalyst design.

lectures.title: Why Milk Does Not Separate Immediately: Colloids, Emulsions, and Tiny Particles
lectures.description: Connects Brownian motion, settling, electrostatic and steric stabilization, emulsifiers, coalescence and ripening to milk, mayonnaise and paint.

lectures.title: Rust Is a Battery You Did Not Ask For: Corrosion and Passivation
lectures.description: Explains anodic and cathodic corrosion regions, oxide films, pitting, galvanic cells, cathodic protection and why geometry governs localized damage.

lectures.title: A Material Remembers How It Was Made: Processing, Structure, and Performance
lectures.description: Explains how casting, work hardening, grain structure, precipitation, quenching, tempering and defects create property differences in chemically similar materials.

lectures.title: Why Solids Have Forbidden Energies: From Atomic Orbitals to Energy Bands
lectures.description: Develops band formation from interacting atomic orbitals, distinguishes occupied states from gaps, and connects carrier transport to optical absorption and indirect-gap behavior.
tag_paths: Electronic states and crystal band structure

lectures.title: A Pinch of Impurity Changes Everything: Doping, Carriers, and the Semiconductor
lectures.description: Explains phosphorus donors, boron acceptors, electron and hole populations, Fermi levels, charge neutrality, processing and the meaning of Hall measurements.

lectures.title: The Junction That Chooses a Direction: Diodes, Barriers, and Transistors
lectures.description: Derives a p-n junction from diffusion and space charge; explains forward and reverse bias, diode nonideality, bipolar transistor action and field-effect gate control.

lectures.title: When Electrons Make Light: The Chemistry of Light-Emitting Diodes
lectures.description: Connects injected electrons and holes to electroluminescence, direct-gap compounds, quantum wells, photon extraction, phosphors and the development of blue LEDs.
tag_paths: Blue LEDs and phosphor-converted white light

lectures.title: When Light Makes Current: The Chemical Architecture of a Solar Cell
lectures.description: Explains light-induced carrier generation and extraction, photovoltaic voltage, recombination, band-gap tradeoffs, current-voltage curves and stability of solar materials.
tag_paths: Photovoltaic efficiency, voltage and fill factor

lectures.title: An Excited Molecule Is a Different Reagent: What a Photon Changes
lectures.description: Distinguishes light absorption, fluorescence, nonradiative relaxation, intersystem crossing, photoisomerization and chemical quantum yield through molecular excited-state competition.
tag_paths: Excited molecular states and relaxation pathways

lectures.title: A Reaction That Borrows a Photon: Photoredox Chemistry and Catalysis
lectures.description: Develops photoredox and energy-transfer pathways, catalytic regeneration, radical chemistry, semiconductor photocatalysis, photon balances and mechanistic experiments.
tag_paths: Photon accounting and photochemical mechanism tests

lectures.title: How a Leaf Spends a Photon: The Chemistry of Photosynthesis
lectures.description: Traces light harvesting, PSII water oxidation, electron transport, proton-motive force, PSI photochemistry, NADPH and the separation of light reactions from carbon fixation.
tag_paths: Pigment energy transfer and reaction-center charge separation
